newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rises on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rises on cold weather.

text.p: A crisp autumn chill pushed spot bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. higher Monday amid thin participation linked to observance of the U.S. Veterans Day holiday, market sources said.
"The biggest drive is the weather," said one Mid-Atlantic power trader, adding, "I think there's some short-covering as well."

The latest forecasts showed Tuesday's temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool to peak in 30s-40s Fahrenheit in the afternoon and to bottom in the 20s at night. The region's weather was predicted to moderate next week.
The 1,031 megawatt (MW) Hope Creek nuclear plant in Salem, N.J., resumed full output Sunday after being shut November 2 for maintenance.
The 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit in Berwick, Pa., was expected to 100 percent production following work on a reactor feed pump.
Power scheduling into eastern PJM from the western district remained restricted due to the reduced operation at the Whitpain substation, north of Philadelphia.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Tuesday was assessed at $27.00-$28.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), with deals heard completed at $27.50-$27.90. Today's quote was up sharply from Friday's $25.00-$25.50.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Tuesday delivery were pegged notationally higher at $15.00-$17.00, up from Friday's $14.00-$15.00.
December PJM electricity for firm delivery during heavy load hours were discussed between $28.50 and $28.85, up from Friday's range of $28.10-$28.30. Transactions reportedly changed hand at $28.75.
January/February 1997 PJM deliveries were valued at $32.10-$32.50, flat from Friday.
March 1997 PJM electricity was pegged at $24.00-$24.60, steady from Friday.
